compilation_policy: Sherlock only; no local Lean/Lake compilation

RV01.description: Unconditional polynomial-time-uniform clean reversible simulation plus exported exact theorem/encoding contract. Not available at planning time; only O02 depends on it.

tasks.title: Freeze the baseline and establish the audit harness
tasks.contract: Create qip/ as an independent pinned Lean project; preserve the existing projects byte-for-byte. Record the actual Git SHA, toolchain, imports and accepted evidence.
proof_steps: Read this plan and current Git status; do not overwrite concurrent edits.
Use module prefixes Quantum.* and QIP.* to avoid existing Space.*, Machine.* and Audit.* collisions. Import one selected baseline closure, never two different definitions with the same module name.
Reuse manifest/audit patterns from bqp-pspace, but change the compilation entry point to require a Sherlock allocation. Separate source-only checks from anything invoking Lean.
Create an audit parser self-test that rejects missing, duplicate and forbidden axiom reports.
tasks.acceptance: Source manifests for both existing projects still pass; a tiny Mathlib-import module and its fresh audit pass on Sherlock.
tasks.do_not: Do not install a new toolchain, run local Lean, rewrite earlier class definitions, or count an imported theorem statement as a proved lemma.

tasks.title: Inventory the pinned Mathlib and proved quantum APIs
tasks.contract: List exact available declarations and missing bridges for matrix order, square roots, tensor products, CP maps, compactness and separation.
proof_steps: Inspect the pinned files listed in Section 4, then use focused #check files on Sherlock.
Record the matrix norm and inner-product conventions, not just matching names.
For each reused project theorem record exact statement, source hash, and transitive axiom report.
tasks.acceptance: The inventory distinguishes already proved, definition-only, stub, proposed and external-pending items.
tasks.do_not: Do not invent Mathlib lemma names or decide an entire theory is absent from one failed keyword search.

tasks.title: Finite registers and tensor reindexing
tasks.contract: Explicit equivalences for ordered register products, associativity, swap, empty registers and qubit blocks.
proof_steps: Use finite nonempty basis types; zero qubits have a one-element basis.
Define reindexing matrices and state maps, and prove inverse, adjoint and composition laws.
Fix one tensor-factor order and prove named equivalences for every other view.
tasks.acceptance: Associativity, swap twice, and adding/removing a zero-qubit register are exact identities.
tasks.do_not: Do not identify differently ordered tensors by informal notation or treat a zero-qubit space as dimension zero.

tasks.title: Positive matrices and finite-dimensional analytic bridges
tasks.contract: Use Mathlib PSD/order and functional calculus to obtain factorization, positive square roots, trace positivity, and the correct Hilbert-space operator norm.
proof_steps: Bridge coordinate functions to EuclideanSpace rather than using the default Pi sup norm.
Prove the needed trace cyclicity, adjoint, conjugation and tensor positivity lemmas.
Factor a PSD matrix as A * Aᴴ; establish the rank-one trace and inner-product identities.
tasks.acceptance: All later order/norm claims resolve to explicit Mathlib structures; tests include non-diagonal complex matrices.
tasks.do_not: Do not create a competing PSD definition or assume positivity is entrywise.

tasks.title: Density operators and effects
tasks.contract: Density operators are PSD matrices with trace one; effects satisfy 0 ≤ E ≤ I; probability is Re(trace(Eρ)).
proof_steps: Prove probability lies in [0,1], complement probabilities sum to one, and affine mixtures preserve states.
Define rank-one pure states and prove normalization equivalence with squared-amplitude sums.
Define the maximally mixed state, including the one-dimensional case.
tasks.acceptance: Pure-state measurement agrees with a direct sum of squared amplitudes.
tasks.do_not: Do not hide normalization, positivity or an acceptance bound in an unproved structure field.

tasks.title: Partial trace and locality
tasks.contract: Partial trace preserves PSD/trace; tensor and local-operation identities are proved with explicit register order.
proof_steps: Start from partialTrace(M)[a,b] = sum_i M[(a,i),(b,i)].
Prove trace, tensor, reindexing and conjugation identities.
Derive marginal invariance under a trace-preserving operation on the other register once Q06 is available; place that corollary in Q06 to avoid an import cycle.
tasks.acceptance: Check a Bell-state marginal, product states and tracing a zero-qubit register.
tasks.do_not: Do not claim a prover can change the verifier-only marginal without a message exchange.

tasks.title: Channels and their compositional API
tasks.contract: A finite-dimensional channel is a linear completely positive trace-preserving map; composition, identity, tensor and local application are channels.
proof_steps: Bridge Mathlib CompletelyPositiveMap on CStarMatrix to the chosen finite matrix representation.
Keep trace preservation as a predicate of that same linear map.
Prove state preservation and no-signalling/local marginal invariance, and represent instruments with outcome-indexed CP maps.
tasks.acceptance: Unitary conjugation, discard, preparation and dephasing are concrete channels.
tasks.do_not: Do not equate positivity with complete positivity or reset verifier-private memory when the prover acts.

tasks.title: Choi representation and Kraus realization
tasks.contract: Prove Choi/map inverse identities, CP iff Choi PSD, and TP iff the output partial trace is the input identity.
proof_steps: Freeze input/output order and matrix-unit conventions.
Prove the forward implication using the unnormalized maximally entangled vector.
Factor a PSD Choi matrix and reshape each factor column into a Kraus operator.
Prove the resulting Kraus sum is the original map and the normalization condition is exact.
tasks.acceptance: Both directions are kernel checked, with input/output dimensions allowed to differ.
tasks.do_not: Do not define CP to mean Choi PSD and omit its equivalence with the channel API; do not normalize the Choi matrix as a density operator.

tasks.title: Finite-dimensional dilation
tasks.contract: Every finite-dimensional channel has an isometric realization with an explicit finite environment; prove unitary extension after padding.
proof_steps: Stack the proved Kraus operators into an isometry.
Prove discarding its environment recovers the channel.
Bound environment dimension and extend the isometry to a unitary only on compatible padded spaces.
tasks.acceptance: The realization works with entangled reference inputs, not just pure inputs of the acted-on system.
tasks.do_not: Do not infer an efficient verifier circuit from existence of an arbitrary channel dilation.

tasks.title: Purification and same-marginal isometries
tasks.contract: Every density operator has a finite purification; purifications of the same marginal are related on a sufficiently large private register.
proof_steps: Use the PSD square root to construct a canonical purification.
Prove its reduced state and normalization.
Prove the equal-marginal isometry/unitary lemma with explicit ancilla dimensions and rank-deficient cases.
tasks.acceptance: Pure, mixed and rank-deficient states are covered; no full-rank assumption leaks out.
tasks.do_not: Do not import Uhlmann as an axiom or use a same-size unitary when the purifying dimensions differ.

tasks.title: Root fidelity and elementary laws
tasks.contract: Use one documented convention: root fidelity F(ρ,σ) = trace(sqrt(sqrt(ρ) σ sqrt(ρ))), a real number in [0,1].
proof_steps: Relate the square-root formula to the trace norm of sqrt(ρ)sqrt(σ).
Prove symmetry, pure-state overlap, diagonal specialization and tensor multiplicativity using finite matrix lemmas.
Keep every occurrence of F and F² distinct in theorem names/statements.
tasks.acceptance: The pure-state formula is absolute inner product, while pure-state acceptance is its square.
tasks.do_not: Do not mix squared fidelity with root fidelity.

tasks.title: Uhlmann theorem with attained optimization
tasks.contract: Maximum overlap over purifications equals root fidelity, with a sufficiently large common environment and an actual maximizing isometry.
proof_steps: Isolate the matrix polar/trace-optimization lemma first.
Prove its upper bound and optimizer construction, including zero singular values.
Translate through vectorization and Q09 to the purification statement; derive monotonicity under partial trace.
tasks.acceptance: The theorem can supply a witness, not merely a supremum inequality.
tasks.do_not: Do not use a supremum as though it were attained or assume a polar factor is invertible.

tasks.title: Two-target fidelity inequality
tasks.contract: For density operators ρ,σ,τ: F(ρ,σ)^2 + F(ρ,τ)^2 ≤ 1 + F(σ,τ). Only this upper bound is mandatory.
proof_steps: Prove the norm bound for the sum of two rank-one projections on unit vectors.
Choose Uhlmann purifications relative to a fixed purification of ρ.
Bound the mutual overlap of those purifications by F(σ,τ).
tasks.acceptance: The inequality has no optimizer or protocol hypotheses and passes its own axiom audit.
tasks.do_not: Do not spend time proving the exact maximum identity unless the upper bound genuinely fails to close Q31.

tasks.title: Protocol syntax and resource accounting
tasks.contract: Finite verifier descriptions explicitly store every private/message register size, alternation schedule, circuit block and output wire. Require a valid designated output qubit even when individual message or private auxiliary registers have zero qubits.
proof_steps: Count a message as one directed transfer; a three-message protocol is P→V, V→P, P→V.
Represent zero-length messages explicitly; all verifier gates use the established H/S/T/X/CNOT semantics.
Define gate count, total wires, communication and serialized-size targets before adding transformations.
tasks.acceptance: Instantiate one-, two-, three- and five-message descriptions; size fields cannot conceal arbitrary functions.
tasks.do_not: Do not call an exchange of two messages one message or omit private/message register boundaries from the description.

tasks.title: Protocol encoding and strict decoder
tasks.contract: A self-delimiting Boolean encoding with decode(encode V) = some V, injectivity and a polynomial encoded-length bound.
proof_steps: Use tagged constructors with explicit arity and bounded wire checks.
Prove parsers retain arbitrary suffixes and reject malformed framing.
Encode all register sizes and each message boundary separately.
tasks.acceptance: Round trip and malformed-input behavior cover empty lists and zero-qubit registers.
tasks.do_not: Do not assume a nested length-prefix/flatten operation is injective; do not reuse the older folded QMA witness/ancilla encoding.

tasks.title: Operational interaction and class definitions
tasks.contract: Define actual interaction, completeness/soundness and independently defined QIP and QIPm. Quantify over all finite private prover memories and legal channels.
proof_steps: A verifier description is generated from x by a total PolyTimeComputable function; prepare any classical x register explicitly.
Keep prover initial memory uncorrelated with verifier-private initialized registers.
Use disjoint yes/no promise sets, with a language embedding (L, complement L).
Bound messages, wire counts, circuit sizes and generator runtime by natural-coefficient polynomials with room for n=0,1.
Define QIPm k by exactly k messages; QIP uses a polynomial bound on the generated message count.
tasks.acceptance: Acceptance is in [0,1]; a dishonest prover has no action on private verifier registers; QIPm 3 ⊆ QIP is proved without compression.
tasks.do_not: Do not define QIP via QIPm 3, via an SDP, or via existence of the desired transformation. Do not bound prover circuit complexity.

tasks.title: Bridge existing circuit semantics
tasks.contract: The density-channel action of each allowed circuit agrees with ShiShallow.runLayered on pure states and preserves the same gate meanings.
proof_steps: Prove each primitive gate identity, then circuit composition and register embedding.
Relate the designated output effect to existing amplitude-sum acceptance.
Prove that an untouched reference register is preserved in the channel statement.
tasks.acceptance: A concrete existing BQP/QMA verifier has identical acceptance in the new semantics.
tasks.do_not: Do not silently change the gate set, layer order or output convention.

tasks.title: Purified strategies and verifier normal forms
tasks.contract: Operational strategies admit pure/isometric private-memory implementations with identical behavior; circuit-described verifiers admit an efficient reversible form.
proof_steps: Separate arbitrary prover dilation from efficient verifier normalization.
For verifier measurements/dephasing, retain coherent outcome copies privately; prove equivalence against arbitrary adversaries.
Allocate needed verifier ancillas at the start and preserve their ownership; pad to a fixed total unitary workspace.
tasks.acceptance: Every normalization direction used later is proved, with unchanged message count or a stated explicit change.
tasks.do_not: Do not let the prover receive purification registers or invoke the unfinished general reversible compiler.

tasks.title: Causal strategy operators
tasks.contract: Define PSD strategy operators with recursive causal partial-trace equations, including the trivial-input first prover action.
proof_steps: Fix register order and define each prefix operator.
Use Q0=1 and Tr_output Qk = Q(k-1) ⊗ I_input, after proved reindexing.
Derive trace normalization and prefix uniqueness; a strategy operator is generally not trace one.
tasks.acceptance: The one-turn case matches Choi channels, and initial state preparation appears as input dimension one.
tasks.do_not: Do not confuse the number of prover turns with the number of exchanged messages.

tasks.title: Strategy representation in both directions
tasks.contract: An operator satisfies the causal constraints iff it is induced by an operational finite-memory strategy; prove a memory-dimension bound.
proof_steps: Forward direction: compose the actual strategy and trace private memory.
Reverse direction: induct on turns using positive factorizations and equal-marginal isometries.
Handle singular prefixes without inserting an inverse unless supported on the correct range.
Show the bounded-memory realization reproduces behavior against every compatible verifier.
tasks.acceptance: This is the first major independently useful theorem; both implications and memory bounds receive fresh audits.
tasks.do_not: Do not assume causal realization or restrict the original prover to the constructed memory bound before proving equivalence.

tasks.title: Verifier testers and interaction pairing
tasks.contract: Construct a PSD accepting tester from the actual verifier; prove operational acceptance equals its trace pairing with the prover strategy operator.
proof_steps: Derive the pairing from vectorization/contraction identities.
Resolve all transpose/conjugation conventions in the definitions.
Prove tester normalization over every legal strategy and compatibility with tensor products.
tasks.acceptance: The formula covers every operational strategy, including those with retained entangled private memory.
tasks.do_not: Do not assume that a partial transpose preserves positivity or write a pairing formula without proving its convention.

tasks.title: Compactness and attained game value
tasks.contract: The operational supremum equals a maximum over the compact strategy-operator set; 0 ≤ value V ≤ 1.
proof_steps: Prove nonempty, closed and bounded causal feasible sets using their fixed trace.
Apply finite-dimensional compactness and continuity of the tester pairing.
Use Q19 to return an actual maximizing strategy and reconcile existential completeness with a value inequality.
tasks.acceptance: All appearances of value=1 later yield a legal perfect prover; no finite-memory bound is assumed externally.
tasks.do_not: Do not replace an existential perfect prover by a bare sSup equation before this theorem.

tasks.title: Tailored strategy SDP and weak duality
tasks.contract: Express the strategy constraints as a finite real-linear map on Hermitian matrices; derive its dual and prove weak duality.
proof_steps: Write the adjoint of every partial-trace constraint explicitly.
Derive the dual from the selected convention, rather than copying incompatible tensor order.
Prove positivity of trace products and the telescoping primal/dual objective bound.
tasks.acceptance: A concrete feasible dual certificate bounds every operational prover through Q19/Q20.
tasks.do_not: Do not run a numerical SDP solver or assume its answer certifies a bound.

tasks.title: Tailored strong duality / approximate certificates
tasks.contract: For every η>0, obtain a feasible dual bound ≤ value V + η. Exact dual attainment is optional unless actually required.
proof_steps: First locate a proved finite-dimensional separation/Slater theorem in pinned Mathlib; instantiate every hypothesis.
If absent, prove the needed finite-dimensional separation argument in a separate file.
Exhibit a strictly feasible causal operator using depolarizing channels and explicitly prove positive definiteness.
Ensure all complex Hermitian variables are treated as a real vector space.
tasks.acceptance: No duality hypothesis survives in the final certificate theorem; strict-feasibility witnesses are actual matrices.
tasks.do_not: Do not assert Slater, strong duality or a solver theorem as an axiom. This is a hard review gate, not a routine automation task.

tasks.title: Product bound against entangled strategies
tasks.contract: Prove value(V⊗W) = value V * value W for all-pass parallel composition; initially the three-message case suffices.
proof_steps: Lower bound: product of actual optimal strategies.
Upper bound: tensor feasible dual certificates and prove each recursive inequality using PSD order.
If certificates are approximate, take η→0 with a proved limiting inequality.
tasks.acceptance: The upper bound quantifies over arbitrary joint strategies, not product strategies.
tasks.do_not: Do not generalize this result to OR acceptance or arbitrary threshold repetition; do not assume independent cheating behavior.

tasks.title: Operational all-pass repetition
tasks.contract: Build k parallel copies with batched messages and all-pass acceptance; preserve three messages and prove value(repeat V k)=value(V)^k for k≥1.
proof_steps: Define the reordered product message registers and batched prover strategy space.
Compile the conjunction of accept bits using proved reversible gate templates.
Prove tensor semantics and induct Q24; record wire/gate/communication counts.
tasks.acceptance: The result applies after perfect completeness and admits a polynomial-time printer in Q38.
tasks.do_not: Do not substitute the existing QMA copy-amplification theorem for this adversarial interactive theorem.

tasks.title: Reject flag and exact half-acceptance witness
tasks.contract: Add a prover-controlled reject option without increasing the number of messages; preserve soundness and permit honest acceptance exactly 1/2 whenever original acceptance is ≥2/3.
proof_steps: Place the flag in an existing prover-to-verifier message; keep the old computation independent of it.
For soundness, trace the flag to obtain an original strategy and use accept_new ≤ accept_old.
For completeness, prepare an independent flag with acceptance weight 1/(2p) for an honest success probability p≥2/3. The prover is unrestricted, so this need not be a finite-gate verifier rotation.
tasks.acceptance: Arbitrary entanglement of a cheating flag is covered; the honest normalization and p>0 proof are explicit.
tasks.do_not: Do not require the verifier to know p or synthesize an arbitrary real rotation.

tasks.title: Bell-test perfect completeness
tasks.contract: A concrete m+2-message transformation has completeness 1 and soundness ≤35/36 from thresholds 2/3 and 1/3.
proof_steps: Implement the Bell-test construction from the reference using the fixed threshold 1/2 and exact H/CNOT gates.
Use Q26 to produce the half-acceptance honest strategy and Q09/unitary extension for its final response.
For soundness, use the unchanged verifier-only marginal and the diagonal fidelity bound; weaken the bound to 1-(1/2-1/3)^2=35/36.
Return actual verifier syntax plus semantic and resource theorems.
tasks.acceptance: Both claims concern this constructed verifier; no arbitrary exact verifier rotations or extra perfect-completeness premise remain.
tasks.do_not: Do not claim the result for variable thresholds without proving their encoding/computation and exact gate realization.

tasks.title: Exact gate adjoints and control macros
tasks.contract: Executable gate-list operations implement adjoints, swaps, controlled branch blocks and zero/all-pass tests in H/S/T/X/CNOT.
proof_steps: Use H⁻¹=H, X⁻¹=X, CNOT⁻¹=CNOT, S⁻¹=S³ and T⁻¹=T⁷. Reverse circuit order as well.
Extract a proved constant Toffoli/controlled-gate template with provenance, or prove its finite matrix identity directly.
Prove exact phase-sensitive action, ancilla cleanup, wire distinctness and per-gate expansion bounds.
tasks.acceptance: Each macro has both semantic equality and a concrete finite encoding; protected control bits cannot be overwritten by returned messages.
tasks.do_not: Do not treat reversing a quantum circuit as requiring the unfinished classical-machine reversible simulation theorem; do not ignore relative phases under control.

tasks.title: Message padding and fixed-register normal form
tasks.contract: Normalize to prover-first odd schedules and uniform message widths; pad to a suitable power-of-two-plus-one message count with identical value.
proof_steps: Use zero-length dummy messages with prescribed ownership transfers.
Initialize, retain and ignore padding in a way that never exposes verifier-private ancillas.
Prove both strategy translations, including dishonest use of all padding qubits.
tasks.acceptance: Message counts 1,2,3,4,5 and empty input are handled; no soundness proof assumes the prover leaves padding zero.
tasks.do_not: Do not use mere register-dimension arithmetic as a proof of operational equivalence.

tasks.title: Cut-state characterization and stitching
tasks.contract: Relate reachable-prefix and accepting-suffix verifier marginals at a fixed cut to legal strategies; derive the fidelity bound needed for halving.
proof_steps: Define the two cut-state sets using actual operational prefixes/suffixes.
Prove purification-based strategy stitching with explicit private-memory enlargement.
Prove branch acceptance is bounded by squared fidelity with an appropriate cut state.
Handle empty feasible sets, zero branch probability, and the final accept projector explicitly; a max over an empty set is not a prover.
tasks.acceptance: Every state used in the soundness argument is related to a legal strategy, and every claimed witness is constructed.
tasks.do_not: Do not replace this step by an abstract cut-consistency hypothesis or postselection available to the prover.

tasks.title: One halving transformation
tasks.contract: For r≥1, transform 2^(r+1)+1 messages into 2^r+1; preserve perfect completeness and prove value(Halve V) ≤(1+sqrt(value V))/2.
proof_steps: Construct the midpoint-state request and forward/backward verifier from the reference, with a private retained challenge bit and a public copy.
For honesty, send the genuine midpoint and use purified prover actions or their inverses.
For soundness, apply Q30 branch bounds and Q12 to the same midpoint marginal chosen before the challenge.
Use only the upper inequality; an exact value identity is not required.
tasks.acceptance: The five-to-three case is proved first, then the indexed general case; challenge timing is present in the operational execution.
tasks.do_not: Do not let the prover choose different midpoint states for the two challenge outcomes or apply the transform recursively below three messages.

tasks.title: Iterated semantic compression
tasks.contract: After padding to M=2^(r+1)+1, r halvings give exactly three messages, completeness 1 and soundness ≤1-ε/M² from soundness ≤1-ε.
proof_steps: Induct on r using the one-step gap loss of at most a factor four.
Track the padded M rather than silently reusing the original unpadded message count.
Record an explicit size recurrence for transformed descriptions to be discharged in Q37/Q39.
tasks.acceptance: r=0 returns a three-message verifier without another halving; every coercion from naturals to reals is explicit.
tasks.do_not: Do not claim polynomial size merely because the iteration count is logarithmic.

tasks.title: Scalar gap bounds and concrete repetition schedule
tasks.contract: Prove the scalar inequalities and an integer schedule K=72*M² for M≥3, δ=1/(36*M²): (1-δ)^K≤1/3.
proof_steps: Prove (1+sqrt(1-ε))/2≤1-ε/4 for 0≤ε≤1.
Prove 4^r≤(2^(r+1)+1)^2 and elementary power-of-two padding bounds.
Prove (1-δ)^k≤1/(1+k*δ) for 0≤δ≤1, by induction or a proved Bernoulli inequality.
Derive K*δ=2 and K polynomially bounded from a polynomial bound on M.
tasks.acceptance: These lemmas are protocol-independent and compile now, before quantum foundations are complete.
tasks.do_not: Do not introduce numerical approximations, logarithm rounding assumptions or an unproved amplification hypothesis.

tasks.title: Concrete classical description-transformer primitives
tasks.contract: Actual TM2 polynomial-time certificates for parsing, list traversal, wire-index arithmetic, copying, concatenation and bounded iteration over encoded protocols.
proof_steps: Reuse small audited transducer/subroutine lemmas, recording their exact input/output encodings.
Return a fixed rejection/default output on malformed input so the generator is total on every Boolean string.
Build a general bounded-loop machine whose finite control does not depend on input length; prove exact output and actual runtime.
tasks.acceptance: Every primitive is a concrete executable machine certificate; clocks include glue, cleanup and output writing.
tasks.do_not: Do not claim Lean recursion is polynomial time, use input-dependent finite label types, or enumerate 2^q amplitudes to print a q-qubit circuit.

tasks.title: Perfect-completeness printer
tasks.contract: A concrete polynomial-time transducer emits exactly the encoding of Q27, including reject-flag layout and the two new messages.
proof_steps: Compose only certified primitives and fixed gate templates.
Prove an exact byte-level output equation, polynomial clock and output-size bound.
tasks.acceptance: Uniformity of the actual Q27 verifier follows from composition with the original generator.
tasks.do_not: Do not prove uniformity of a different verifier with merely the same asymptotic size.

tasks.title: Halving and padding printers
tasks.contract: Certified transducers for message padding, midpoint layout, reverse/adjoint blocks and challenge routing.
proof_steps: Parse full register metadata; calculate offsets with the proved arithmetic primitives.
Print branch circuits with bounded control macros and retain a protected challenge record.
Prove exact encoding agreement and per-transformation size/time inequalities.
tasks.acceptance: The printer handles all valid parity/base cases and returns a specified result for invalid encodings.
tasks.do_not: Do not assume the unfinished reversible-machine generator provides this description transformer.

tasks.title: Uniform iterated compression
tasks.contract: A total polynomial-time machine pads once and repeatedly halves until exactly three messages; its bytes equal Q32.
proof_steps: Implement bounded doubling to select the padded count, then a counted halving loop.
Prove the loop invariant relating the current bytes, message count and semantic transform.
Solve the actual description-size recurrence, including wire-address encodings and branch-control growth.
Prove a polynomial bound in the original encoded length, not in Hilbert-space dimension.
tasks.acceptance: No uniformity or loop-runtime premise remains; constant-factor-per-stage growth is justified for the selected representation.
tasks.do_not: Do not reparse/synthesize exponential matrices or assume an arbitrary polynomial factor repeated log times is polynomial.

tasks.title: Uniform parallel repetition
tasks.contract: A concrete polynomial-time printer emits K batched copies with AND acceptance and exactly three messages.
proof_steps: Compute K from the padded message count using a fixed polynomial arithmetic program.
Relabel disjoint copies, batch each round and append the proved all-pass circuit.
Prove exact encoded output and polynomial overhead in K and original description size.
tasks.acceptance: The actual resulting verifier has the product semantics established in Q25.
tasks.do_not: Do not use sequential repetition, which would increase message count.

tasks.title: Compose family resources and uniformity
tasks.contract: Assemble one transformed family with a real TM2 generator and explicit natural-coefficient polynomial bounds on every resource.
proof_steps: Compose the exact printer equations in the same order as the semantic transforms.
Derive padded M and K bounds from the original family bounds.
Include input length zero/one, width, gate count, all message widths and total encoded output length.
tasks.acceptance: The family can be inserted into QIPm 3 directly without supplying compiler/runtime/gap hypotheses.
tasks.do_not: Do not substitute a polynomial-space generator for a polynomial-time generator.

tasks.title: Public class equality
tasks.contract: Prove ShiQIP.qip_eq_qip3 : ShiQIP.QIP = ShiQIP.QIPm 3, for the independently fixed classes.
proof_steps: Forward: instantiate the perfect-complete, padded/compressed, all-pass-repeated family.
Use δ=1/(36*M²), K=72*M² and Q33 to finish soundness; perfect completeness implies the required 2/3.
Reverse: use the constant polynomial message bound for a three-message family.
Derive the language-level statement by the promise embedding, rather than redefining existing BQP/PP/PSPACE.
tasks.acceptance: An independent example has exactly the equality type; no helper assumptions or uninstantiated typeclass law fields remain.
tasks.do_not: Do not cite QIP=PSPACE, IP=PSPACE, BQP⊆PSPACE or the desired equality to prove this theorem.

tasks.title: Final clean build and semantic audit
tasks.contract: A source-matched clean Sherlock build and exact-type/transitive-axiom audit certify the complete theorem graph.
proof_steps: Build all project dependencies without reused project objects against pinned Mathlib libraries.
Audit the endpoint, operational/strategy equivalence, Uhlmann, duality, product bound, compression and all printer certificates.
Review definitions and quantifiers independently of axioms: adversarial memory, uniformity, dimensions, message count and class thresholds.
Save sources, hashes, logs, objects and allocation metadata before releasing node scratch.
tasks.acceptance: All reports present; allowed axioms only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound; zero sorryAx; zero reused project objects in the final build.
tasks.do_not: Do not describe an incremental/local check as a clean Sherlock build or equate axiom cleanliness with correctness of the class definitions.

tasks.title: One-message compatibility with the existing QMA semantics
tasks.contract: At a fixed input, identify one-message verification with optimization over a witness state; connect the corrected QMAU semantics where encodings permit.
proof_steps: Read Def_ShiClassQMAU and distinguish it from the older folded-uniformity class.
Prove pure-vs-mixed witness equivalence by linearity/spectral decomposition.
Prove only the class inclusions for which a real uniform generator translation is available.
tasks.acceptance: Exact names/types state whether the result is semantic, a class inclusion, or a full class equality.
tasks.do_not: Do not claim ShiClassQMA.QMA equals the new QIPm 1 merely because textbook QMA=QIP(1).

tasks.title: Input-uniformity model bridge using future reversible simulation
tasks.contract: Optional bridge between input-dependent verifier generators and unary-length uniform circuits that process x internally.
proof_steps: Wait for an audited, exported unconditional reversible simulation theorem.
Prove a uniform universal evaluator for the bounded encoded verifier circuits, including controlled gate templates.
Compose coherent description generation, evaluation and cleanup, with separate proof of all size/uniformity bounds.
tasks.acceptance: This is an additional compatibility theorem; the primary equality Q40 must not wait on it.
tasks.do_not: Do not assume reversible simulation alone also supplies a universal circuit or this model equivalence.
